assign.outcome:
**Site diff lands** — one command that shoots the site before and after a landing and says what changed, so the owner stops finding breaks one page at a time.

`node public/framework/ext/DesignTool/diff/site-diff.mjs baseline --out <dir>` shoots 40 representative pages (one of each kind: realms, paging, layouts, blog, notes, platform, size/spacing/controls) at 1280 and 3440, saves a PNG per page-per-width plus `manifest.json`.
`node site-diff.mjs compare --baseline <dir> --out <dir>` re-shoots the SAME set (read out of the baseline's own manifest) and reports pixels changed, new console errors, new sideways scroll — worst page first — in `report.json` and a stdout table. Exits non-zero only when something got worse.

The framework's live clock (`.panel-t-clock`) is painted flat grey before every shot on both sides, so it never shows as "changed".

Self-test against the shared server: baseline 40×2 in 13.1s, 0 console errors. Compare against itself: 0 of 40 pages changed (the mask holds pixel-exact, even on the clock's own page), 18.4s. Compare with `--inject "a{text-decoration:underline!important}"`: 40 of 40 changed, correctly ranked — the link-heaviest pages (paging library, blog front, home) land at the top, the link-lightest (design/size, design/controls) at the bottom. 19.8s. Both real runs are well under the 90s budget.
